title: Three perfect days in Las Vegas: Grand Prix weekend
dek: Red rock and downtown on qualifying day, Hoover Dam before the race, and a slow Sunday of brunch, flowers and Oz once the barriers come down. A plan for working with the Formula 1 closures, not against them.

hero.caption: The Las Vegas Strip, which becomes part of a Formula 1 street circuit on Thursday, Friday and Saturday nights.

intro:
This is the weekend the Strip turns into a racetrack. The Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix runs Thursday to Saturday, Nov. 19 to 21, and every session is held after dark: practice on Thursday at 4:30 and 8 p.m., final practice and qualifying on Friday at the same times, and the race itself at 8 p.m. Saturday. From 1 p.m. on each of those days, the roads that form the circuit close: Las Vegas Boulevard between Sands and Harmon avenues, Koval Lane, Harmon, Sands and part of Flamingo Road. They reopen after midnight, and not until 2 a.m. after the race.

That rhythm shapes this plan. If you have race tickets, you will spend your evenings at the track; if you don't, the city is still very much open, and the trick is to be on the right side of the barriers by early afternoon. So Friday heads west to Red Rock Canyon, Summerlin and downtown, Saturday goes out to Hoover Dam and Boulder City and comes back to the South Strip for an early dinner before the lights go out, and Sunday, with the roads open again, takes in the Center Strip at an easy pace.

Expect a full city. Race weekend is one of the most expensive hotel weekends of the year, although rates have cooled since the first race, and with Thanksgiving on Thursday, Nov. 26, the busy stretch runs straight into the holiday week. Downtown and off-Strip hotels are the easiest way to keep costs down. The weather is on your side: mid-November brings mild days, cool nights and a sunset around 4:30, so plan outdoor time for the morning.

days.title: Friday: Red Rock, Summerlin and downtown
days.intro: Qualifying day. Spend it west and north of the circuit: sandstone in the morning, lunch in Summerlin, desert gardens in the afternoon and dinner on Fremont East.

stops.name: Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area
stops.area: Red Rock Canyon, west of Summerlin
stops.wiki: Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area
stops.text: Half an hour west of the Strip, the 13-mile scenic drive loops past red and cream sandstone cliffs, with trailheads every few miles. On a cool November morning, pick one short hike and one overlook rather than trying to see it all, and keep the rest of the morning for the drive itself. It is the quickest way to remember that Las Vegas sits in a real desert. Practical note: from Oct. 1 to May 31, a timed-entry reservation is required for the scenic drive between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m.; in November the drive is open 6 a.m. to 5 p.m. Book your slot ahead.

stops.name: Honey Salt
stops.text: On the way back into town, Elizabeth Blau and chef Kim Canteenwalla's neighborhood restaurant is where Summerlin goes for a long lunch. The menu is seasonal comfort food with lighter and vegan options alongside; the Backyard Favorite Burger has made Las Vegas Weekly's list of the city's best. It is a relaxed room, a world away from race weekend. Practical note: Friday lunch runs 11:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., with happy hour from 3 at the bar and on the patio.

stops.name: Springs Preserve
stops.text: The city began here, at the springs that drew travelers to the valley, and the preserve tells that story across museums, desert gardens and walking trails. It is also home to the Nevada State Museum, with its natural and human history of the state. In the mild afternoon the gardens are at their best, and it is a quiet counterweight to the noise building on the Strip. Practical note: open Thursday to Monday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., with last entry at 3, so arrive by 2.

stops.name: Carson Kitchen
stops.text: Carson Kitchen helped turn the streets east of Fremont into a place locals go to eat, and it has kept its following for more than a decade. The format is shared plates: order a few for the table, plus something from the bar, and finish with dessert. It is lively, informal and close to everything downtown. Practical note: downtown is well away from the circuit closures, so getting here on Friday evening is easy, but book ahead, since race weekend fills the off-Strip tables too.

stops.name: Fremont Street Experience
stops.text: A short walk from dinner, the five blocks under the Fremont Street canopy are old Las Vegas at full volume: the Golden Nugget, the Four Queens and Binion's, street performers, zip-liners overhead and the light shows on the giant screen above. It is the right place to be while qualifying plays out on the Strip, since you can hear about the result from any casino bar without fighting the crowds. Practical note: it is free and open all night; the Deuce bus runs back to the Strip, though on race-week routes.

days.title: Saturday: Hoover Dam, then race night
days.intro: Leave early for the dam and Boulder City, and be back on the South Strip by mid-afternoon, before the circuit closes off the center of town.

stops.name: Hoover Dam
stops.text: The concrete arch that holds back the Colorado River is still one of the great sights of the American West, and it is better in person than any photograph suggests. Walk across the top of the dam between Nevada and Arizona, look down the 726-foot face, and take a tour inside if you want to see the generators and tunnels. Practical note: you will need a car for the day; the visitor center sells the tours, and security checks on the approach road take a little time, so go early.

stops.name: Mike O'Callaghan–Pat Tillman Memorial Bridge
stops.text: The bridge that carries U.S. 93 across Black Canyon has a pedestrian walkway on its north side, and it gives you the one view the dam itself cannot: the whole structure from above and downstream, with Lake Mead's intake towers behind it. The walk out takes only a few minutes from the parking area on the Nevada side, up a set of ramps and stairs. Practical note: there is little shade and the walkway is exposed to wind, so bring a layer and water.

stops.name: Boulder Dam Brewing Co.
stops.text: Boulder City was built to house the dam's workers, and it is still a small town with a walkable main street, one of the few in Nevada without casinos. The brewery on Nevada Way is a relaxed lunch stop: beer brewed on site, pub food and a patio for a mild November day. Walk the few blocks of the historic district afterward. Practical note: it is about 10 minutes from the dam and 30 minutes back to the South Strip; aim to leave by 2 p.m. to beat race-day traffic.

stops.name: Welcome to Fabulous Las Vegas sign
stops.wiki: Welcome to Fabulous Las Vegas sign
stops.text: The 1959 sign at the south end of the Strip is the photo everyone wants, and Saturday afternoon on the way back from Boulder City is a good time to get it, since it sits south of the circuit and away from the closures. The median has a small parking lot, and there is usually a short line for the classic shot under the sign. Practical note: from here, go straight to your hotel or dinner; after 1 p.m., crossing the circuit gets hard, so plan to stay on one side of it for the evening.

stops.name: Best Friend
stops.text: Roy Choi's Koreatown restaurant has been at Park MGM since 2018, and it is still loud, colorful and a lot of fun, with a club feel in the main room. Order the Kogi short rib tacos and Korean wings, a banchan sampler and the kimchi fried rice. Park MGM sits just south of the Harmon Avenue edge of the circuit and is one of the official rideshare pickup points this weekend. Practical note: book an early table so you can be settled by the 8 p.m. start.

stops.name: Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix
stops.text: Fifty laps of the Strip at night, past Caesars, Bellagio and Sphere, at speeds the boulevard was never built for. If you have a ticket, the main grandstand at East Harmon faces the start-finish line, and the T-Mobile Zone at Sphere looks over the chicane; general admission standing room is the cheapest way in. If not, find a bar or a room with a view and listen for the engines carrying across the city. Practical note: there is no re-entry to the track after 7 p.m., and roads do not reopen until 2 a.m.

days.title: Sunday: the Center Strip, reopened
days.intro: The barriers start to come down overnight. Take the morning slowly, then walk the middle of the Strip for brunch, flowers, Oz and Thai food, and finish under a circus tent.

stops.name: Bardot Brasserie
stops.text: Michael Mina's Paris-style brasserie at Aria does one of the Strip's best weekend brunches, in a room of dark wood, mosaic floors and banquettes. Start with the pastry basket and a green juice, then the crêpe madame, croissant Benedict or the steamed mussels with fries; there is caviar and sparkling wine if the race went your way. Practical note: reserve ahead through Aria's restaurant pages; from here, the Bellagio Conservatory is a 15-minute walk north through the resorts.

stops.name: Bellagio Conservatory & Botanical Gardens
stops.text: Bellagio's glass-roofed conservatory changes its display five times a year, and this fall's autumn scene, unveiled in September, is built from about 500,000 autumn-colored leaves and 37,800 flowers and plants. Look for forest animals made from manzanita and driftwood, a New England seaside cabin and a 687-pound pumpkin. It is free and open around the clock. Practical note: after the conservatory, step out front for the fountain show on the lake, which runs through the afternoon.

stops.name: The Wizard of Oz at Sphere
stops.text: The 1939 film reimagined for Sphere's wraparound screen has become one of the city's biggest draws, and it plays four times on Sunday. Expect a 75-minute cut, expanded scenes that use the full dome, and physical effects including wind and light indoor rain; the tornado is the centerpiece. Purists object to some of the edits and AI enhancements, but the scale is unlike anything else. Practical note: Sphere sits in the middle of the F1 setup, so walk over from the Venetian and allow extra time.

stops.name: Lotus of Siam
stops.text: Saipin Chutima's Northern Thai restaurant, run today with her daughter Penny Chua, reopened in May in the Sahara Avenue strip-mall space where it began. Order the khao soi, the garlic prawns and nam prik ong, and look at the throwback menu of dishes from the early years. Chutima's James Beard award is one reason people come; the cooking is why they come back. Practical note: dinner is served Wednesday to Sunday, 5 to 10 p.m., with reservations on OpenTable.

stops.name: Absinthe
stops.text: Spiegelworld's circus-cabaret plays in a small tent in front of Caesars Palace, so the acrobats perform within a few feet of every seat. Between the hand-balancing and the roller-skating acts, the Gazillionaire and his assistant deliver a stream of rude jokes, and the 80 minutes go quickly. It is the best way to end a weekend: close up, funny and nothing to do with cars. Practical note: Sunday shows are at 7 and 9 p.m.; it is for ages 18 and up.

stay.name: Waldorf Astoria Las Vegas
stay.text: No casino and no smoke: the Waldorf occupies a slim tower next to Aria, with a 23rd-floor lobby bar looking up the Strip. It sits just south of the circuit's Harmon Avenue edge, so you can walk to Bardot for Sunday brunch and to Park MGM for dinner without crossing a barrier.

stay.name: Bellagio
stay.text: The fountains, the conservatory and the lake: Bellagio is the Strip's classic address, and on race weekend it sits right on the circuit, so fountain-view rooms look over the track. Expect race-weekend rates and crowds, but also everything on Sunday's plan within a walk.

stay.name: El Cortez
stay.text: Opened in 1941 and still standing on Fremont Street, El Cortez is the downtown classic at downtown prices, around the corner from Carson Kitchen. Downtown hotels run far below the Strip on race weekend, and the closures are miles away.

events.name: Formula 1 practice
events.text: The first two practice sessions open race week; Two Friends and Ja Rule play the T-Mobile Stage in the zone at Sphere.

events.name: Golden Knights vs. Dallas Stars
events.text: The Knights' only home game of the weekend, against a Central Division rival, on the first night of track action.

events.name: Qualifying and Disclosure
events.when: Fri., final practice 4:30 p.m., qualifying 8 p.m.
events.where: Las Vegas Strip Circuit; T-Mobile Stage at Sphere
events.text: Qualifying sets Saturday's grid; Disclosure plays a DJ set with Gorgon City on the fan-zone stage for ticket holders.

events.name: Marc Anthony: Vegas… My Way!
events.text: The last two dates of the salsa star's fall residency, on the North Strip and outside the circuit, with late-night sets at Nowhere Lounge afterward.

events.name: Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix
events.text: The fourth race on the Strip, under the lights. Sean Paul and Natasha Bedingfield play the T-Mobile Stage beforehand; roads reopen at 2 a.m.

events.name: F1 Afterparty: Backstreet Boys
events.text: The first official post-race show, for race ticket holders who buy the add-on or a package.

events.name: The Wizard of Oz at Sphere
events.text: With no race on Sunday, Sphere returns to a full day of its reimagined 1939 film.

know: **From the airport.** Harry Reid International (LAS) is just south of the Strip, usually 10 to 20 minutes by taxi or rideshare. This weekend, expect detours and surge pricing from early afternoon; designated rideshare pickups near the circuit are at Virgin Hotels, Tuscany Suites, Park MGM and the Hughes Center. Flights out fill on Sunday, so leave extra time.

**The 1 p.m. rule.** On Thursday, Friday and Saturday, circuit roads close in stages from 12:30 p.m., fully by 1:45. They reopen at 12:30 a.m. Friday, 12:01 a.m. Saturday and 2 a.m. Sunday. Treat 1 p.m. as the last reliable time to cross the Strip between Sands and Harmon; pedestrian bridges near the track are restricted during sessions. Koval Lane stays closed between Rochelle and Harmon through Nov. 23.
**Take the Monorail.** It runs nonstop, 24 hours a day, from Tuesday morning to 3 a.m. Monday, Nov. 23, every 4 to 8 minutes, from MGM Grand to SAHARA behind the east side of the Strip.
**Buses on race routes.** The Deuce and Routes 119, 202 and 203 run special race-week routes from Nov. 17 to 25, and many Strip stops are closed. Check the rideRTC alerts page before you set out.
**Hotel demand.** Race weekend is among the priciest of the year, and Thanksgiving week follows directly. Downtown and off-Strip hotels run well below the Strip; book now and read cancellation terms.

**You need a car for two mornings.** Red Rock Canyon requires a timed-entry reservation between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m.; Hoover Dam and Boulder City are 30 to 45 minutes southeast. Neither has useful transit.
**Short days, cool nights.** The sun sets around 4:30 p.m. in late November and desert nights are chilly; bring a layer for the grandstands.
**Tipping.** 18 to 20 percent at sit-down restaurants, a dollar or two a drink at the bar, and something for housekeeping, valets and bell staff.
